title: Out-of-order arrival: of two parties, one says yes to Thursday; then an older message of hers (written 45 minutes before the yes) arrives, stepping out. Order by time: the yes is her latest word, so it stands.
source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee). The decline at event 1 carries the earlier timestamp (2026-11-16T14:20:44.000Z) and arrives second; the state sorts each party's messages by time, so in B and C the yes renders as her latest; A sees the late message appended with its own timestamp. An event's `capture` is the expected path's carry, not a recorded run: it is used only when a later event runs on its own.

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find 45 minutes for the three of us
this week for the design review? Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up 45 minutes with you both on a Meet link. Here are times that work on his side:

- Tue, Nov 17, 3:30pm to 4:15pm ET
- Wed, Nov 18, 12:00pm to 12:45pm ET
- Thu, Nov 19, 10:00am to 10:45am ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

sent.summary: Offered three times on a Meet link, Bob in cc.
